item.title: Trump's racist post about Obamas is deleted after backlash despite White House earlier defending it
item.description: WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump’s racist social media post featuring former President Barack Obama and his wife, Michelle Obama, as primates in a jungle was deleted Friday after a backlash from both Republicans and Democrats who criticized the video as offensive. item.title: New Kansas crime law raises fine for buying sex, makes more car thefts a felony
item.description: Kansas Gov. Laura Kelly signed a bill meant to strengthen laws against multiple crimes.

item.title: Man pleads no contest in fatal Wichita shooting
item.description: Ricardo Talavera pleaded no contest on Friday to reckless involuntary manslaughter and interference with law enforcement by concealing, altering or destroying evidence.

item.title: Kansas drive-in saved thanks to funds for new projector
item.description: Kanopolis Drive-In on Wednesday said that it has secured funding for a new 4K laser projector, which will bring brighter movies and images this summer.

item.title: Childcare resource site rolls out in two Kansas counties
item.description: The website includes a list of childcare providers in the county who are licensed through the Kansas Department of Health and Environment.

item.title: Jury awards $35M in medical malpractice suit, family of Newton child only gets $1M
item.description: A Sedgwick County jury awarded a Newton family $35 million in a medical malpractice case, but due to Kansas law, they will only receive about $1 million.

item.title: Hutchinson voters to decide on proposed sales tax in March
item.description: Voters in Hutchinson will soon decide whether to approve a proposed 0.75% city sales tax.

item.title: KSN Courtside: Basketball scores and highlights
item.description: Kansas high school basketball season is underway. KSN’s Michael Emami and Asia Cymone Smith has you covered with scores and highlights from Wichita and around the state.

item.title: Storm Track 3 Forecast: Temperatures climb far above normal over the weekend
item.description: Chief Meteorologist Lisa Teachman says to expect a quiet stretch of weather over the next few days, then the pattern turns more active late next week.
